title: Unplug a latched Ethernet cable from a desktop modem
instruction: Unplug the Ethernet connector from the desktop modem and leave both resting on the counter.
context: Unplugging an Ethernet cable from a home modem or router is an everyday chore, and routine work for computer support specialists: the plug's locking tab must be held down while pulling, and pulling without it drags or tips the loose modem.
setup: Two loose objects on the station counter: (1) a vertical 4-port Gigabit desktop cable modem matching the Motorola MB8600 exterior envelope at x = 0.280 m, y = +0.042 m (57 x 184 x 200 mm housing on a 74 x 184 x 7 mm base foot, 0.523 kg, friction 0.55), with its upper LAN 1 RJ45 receptacle cavity centered at z = 118.0 mm above the counter on the -Y rear bezel (world y = -0.0500 m) behind a 1.8 mm upper locking lip, below the visual F-coax barrel and above LAN 2 to LAN 4; and (2) an IEC 60603-7 8P8C RJ45 modular plug with Stewart SS-39200-085 boot envelope and rigid Cat6 strain-relief collar (11.68 mm plug width, 6.60 mm tongue height, 36.07 mm plug-and-boot length plus a 14.0 x 6.0 mm collar, total mass 0.026 kg, friction 0.75) seated 13.0 mm inside LAN 1 at x = 0.280 m, y = -0.0545 m, z = TOP + 0.1180 m. A front-hinged spring-return top locking tab (0.12 Nm/rad, explicit per-step spring target) engages 1.15 mm behind the bezel lip until depressed. Port heights, tab stiffness, catch overlap, and omitted cable tail are estimates. Real-trial cable: 1.0 m Cat6 UTP patch cord with the tested plug in LAN 1 and the far end free. Let it descend behind the modem to the counter near (0.28,-0.20)m, then lay it slack along +x to (0.58,-0.20), around a 100 mm-radius U toward(0.58,-0.40), and back toward(0.39,-0.40). No other end is connected or tensioned; remaining slack lies on the counter. The flexible length beyond the simulated collar is omitted in simulation.
scoring: End-state binary score. 1.0 when the intact RJ45 connector is fully disconnected (no plug collider occupies the LAN 1 insertion cavity), the modem is upright within 5 degrees with its base within 3 mm of the counter, the plug rests within 3 mm of the counter, both pad midpoints and all four independent jaw endpoints are at least 80 mm from every modem and plug collider, the tab angle remains within [-0.02, 0.22] radians, and every sampled modem/plug/tab point moves under 1 mm over the final 21 samples at 20 Hz. Any counter location, side, orientation or modem distance is equally valid; no 35 mm separation or rearward-region condition. Otherwise 0.0; no placement-based partial credit.
reset_notes: Depress the RJ45 locking tab, push the plug 13.0 mm into the upper LAN 1 port until the barb clicks behind the bezel lip, and set the upright modem at x = 0.280 m, y = +0.042 m with its ports facing -Y. Simulation reset restores the fixed layout with object_jitter = 0. Use the same 1.0 m cord and slack U-shaped starting route every trial; photograph the route at reset. Final connector placement anywhere on the counter counts equally.
fidelity: Exterior follows Motorola MB8600 (57 x 184 x 200 mm, 0.523 kg), IEC 60603-7 tongue, and Stewart SS-39200-085 36.07 mm boot; internal CAD is not claimed. Rigid ABS/PC bodies; flexible cable tail beyond the 14 mm collar, pin wipe, and click acoustics are omitted. Port heights, tab stiffness (0.12 Nm/rad), damping (0.004 Nms/rad), 1.15 mm barb overlap, and friction (0.55/0.75) are engineering estimates; torsional patches are bounded to collider half-widths.
